messages.subject: Instructions to advise - Hartwell Pharma v Cryovance (cold-chain)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Harriet,

Please find our instructions to advise on merits and quantum, and in particular on the prospects of defeating Cryovance's reliance on the clause 11.3 limitation cap. Enclosed are the Services Agreement, both temperature data-logger records, the two QP stability assessments, and the LBA correspondence. The central feature is that the second excursion occurred after Cryovance had been warned of the first.

Grateful for your view on whether to resist any preliminary-issue application on 11.3.

Kind regards,
Tom Gallagher

--
Whitfield Carter LLP, 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Instructions to advise - Hartwell Pharma v Cryovance (cold-chain)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Tom,

My advice is attached. In short: breach is strong; the case turns on clause 11.3. I prefer the UCTA reasonableness route to the construction route, and I assess prospects of defeating or substantially limiting 11.3 at around 65-70%. The repeated failure after notice should be characterised as a reckless disregard of the GDP obligations. I would resist a preliminary issue on 11.3 - it is fact-sensitive and should be tried with the facts of the second excursion.

Harriet
